correctness.rationale: For each integer p>=2 the rational orbit u_j=2^(p-1-j)/(2^p-1) has p distinct states. Selected vs excluded ordinary-to-stubborn distances are integer multiples of 1/(2^p-1), disjoint by parity and strict spacing; symmetric unions of open intervals radius 1/[100(2^p-1)] ensure the required left-trust-only itinerary for p-1 steps and right-trust-only for the last. Actual averaging gives u_(j+1)=u_j/2 and final (u_(p-1)+1)/2=u_0. In a uniform small neighborhood each affine step has slope 1/2, so the return map contracts exactly 2^-p and yields open local basin; no one-/two-agent symmetric self-confident system can cycle because ordinary distances to sole stubborn opinions cannot increase. Independent exact rational itinerary and contraction checks for p=2..24 support all-p proof.
